verdict.rationale: Ramp ships multiple event-triggered automations (auto top-up when balance drops, hotel rebooking when price drops $50+, dynamic approval routing, auto-categorization/coding, fraud flagging) and a webhooks system explicitly positioned as 'the canonical surface for any event-driven workflow' for 'notify me when X happens' triggers. However, these are largely fixed, vendor-defined automations rather than a general-purpose user-configurable rule builder (if-condition-then-action) that an AI-native user could freely define; custom event-driven logic requires building a webhook consumer rather than a native no-code rules UI. Missing for 10: evidence of a native no-code/if-then rule-builder interface for arbitrary custom triggers-and-actions, and independent confirmation of these automations working end-to-end in practice.
